subject: ventures/xer-schedule-check
professional: a planning and scheduling professional (AACE PSP) who reviews contractors' P6 updates against the DCMA 14-point assessment

evidence.correctness: Own Python counter on raw TASK/TASKPRED/CALENDAR tables (scratchpad indep/dcma.py, written this session) reproduces DCMA points 1-8 exactly on Expressway, CCA, hotel and terminal (40 of 40 counts). With a synthetic baseline (indep/mkbase.py: CCA with every not-started activity's early finish moved to 2011-09-01), an independent count gives due 13,228, missed 11,694 (88.4%), BEI 0.116; `node cli.mjs CCA.xer --baseline cca-base.xer` and the page give the same. CPLI on a two-activity hand case (20 working days of path, must-finish 5 days earlier) = 0.75 by hand and from assess(). CLI: 14,268 of 14,270 CCA open activities agree with P6's stored early/late finish and float. Kept at 3, not 4: points with nothing to measure still score PASS (defect 0).
evidence.completeness: Baseline file input exists on the page (#dcma-base) and CLI (--baseline) and changes points 11 and 14 as documented; one-line CLI errors; page scorecard, details and extra checks render on CCA in 2.4 s. 628 tests across ~80 test files pass.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 628 pass, 0 fail, 4.7 s. On arrival the same nine mutants as the prior audit were rerun with quality_mutate.py: 7 of 9 survived (unchanged since 2026-11-19). This PR adds dcma-thresholds.test.mjs; after it, the four DCMA threshold mutants (high float, negative float, CPLI, BEI numerator) are caught; the point-12 margin, SF backward lag and start-float mutants still survive. Score is the state on arrival.
evidence.craft: Read dcma.mjs (613 lines), cli.mjs error paths, index.html wiring for #dcma-base. CLI now prints one-line errors for a missing file, a non-XER file and `--project` with no value (exits 1/1/2). Page at 375 px: scrollWidth 375, no console errors, no requests leave the page (Playwright, page.route).
evidence.claims: FAQ (visible and FAQPage JSON-LD) now says planned dates stand in for the baseline only on started or finished work, and that a baseline file can be opened: true per P6 behaviour and the CCA count. README no longer claims unit tests for progress override, start float, lag calendars or mandatory constraints; its 'no unit test covers them' line was slightly stale (progress override has one), corrected in this PR. No-warranty and not-affiliated lines present. Remaining: the headline 'N of 14 pass' counts vacuous passes (defect 0).
evidence.fitness: A scheduler reviewing a monthly update can now open the update and the baseline XER together and get missed tasks and BEI against the baseline, which was the main gap; activity lists per point export to CSV. The job of a DCMA review is finishable in the browser without a P6 seat.
evidence.domain: Compared against the DCMA 14-point assessment as practised (BEI = finished to date / baseline-due; missed tasks against the baseline finish). The baseline fix brings 11 and 14 into line. Departures left: n/a points scored as passes, every start/finish milestone exempt from point 1 rather than only the project start and finish, and LOE/WBS predecessors counted in points 2-4 (698 links on CCA; FS share 84.0% vs 85.0%). Each is medium or low; a PSP would sign the activity lists and the 11/14 numbers with a baseline loaded, and would discount the pass tally.

verdict: The prior audit's high defect is closed: a baseline XER can now be opened on the page or passed with --baseline, and on a synthetic CCA baseline missed tasks (11,694 of 13,228) and BEI (0.116) match an independent count exactly. DCMA points 1-8 match my own counter on 40 of 40 counts across four public files, CPLI matches a hand case, and 14,268 of 14,270 CCA activities agree with P6's stored dates. Five of nine prior defects are closed (FAQ, README test claims, CLI errors and rounding, baseline). It still misses the bar on verification: on arrival the same 7 of 9 seeded threshold and CPM-branch bugs survived the 628 tests (this PR's new tests now catch 4 of them; point 12's margin, the SF backward lag and start-float type still survive). Points with nothing to measure still count as passes in the headline tally, and two low DCMA population departures remain; those are listed in NEXT.md.
